### Dependencies
- [ ] 🔴 SUP-001 **Lockfile committed and used:** `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `poetry.lock` or `requirements.txt` with pinned versions. CI installs with `npm ci` / `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (not a plain `npm install` that can drift).
- [ ] 🔴 SUP-002 **No suspicious or unknown packages:** every dependency is real, widely used and maintained. Check for typosquats (e.g. `reqeusts`, `lodahs`), very new packages with few downloads, and packages added by AI tools that don't match their purpose.
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-003 **Install scripts reviewed:** dependencies with `preinstall`/`postinstall` scripts are known and needed. Consider `npm config set ignore-scripts true` for CI where possible, or an allow-list.
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-004 **No dependencies from Git URLs, tarballs or personal forks** unless intentional and pinned to a commit.
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-005 **Unused dependencies removed** (`npx depcheck` or similar): fewer packages, fewer risks.
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-006 **Private package scopes protected:** internal package names are scoped (`@company/…`) and registries configured, so a public package with the same name can't be installed instead (dependency confusion).

### CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions and similar)
- [ ] 🔴 SUP-007 **Third-party actions pinned to a full commit SHA** (not `@main` or `@v1`), at least for actions that touch secrets or deploy.
- [ ] 🔴 SUP-008 **No dangerous triggers:** `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` workflows never check out and run code from a fork with access to secrets.
- [ ] 🔴 SUP-009 **Least-privilege tokens:** `permissions:` set per workflow (default `contents: read`). Deploy tokens are scoped to one project, and short-lived OIDC credentials are used for cloud deploys where possible.
- [ ] 🔴 SUP-010 **Secrets never printed or exposed:** no `echo $SECRET`, no secrets in build logs, artifacts, caches or client bundles. Secrets aren't available to pull requests from forks.
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-011 **No untrusted input in shell steps:** PR titles, branch names and issue text aren't interpolated directly into `run:` commands (`${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}`). Pass them through environment variables instead.
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-012 **Production deploys need the main branch and passing checks.** Environment protection rules or required reviewers for production.
- [ ] 🟢 SUP-013 **Build provenance / signed artifacts** for packages or containers you publish.

### Third-party scripts in the browser
- [ ] 🔴 SUP-014 **Every external script is known and needed:** list each `<script src>` from another domain (analytics, chat, A/B testing, tag managers, widgets). Each one can read the page, including forms and tokens.
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-015 **Subresource Integrity (SRI)** (`integrity="sha384-…"` plus `crossorigin`) on scripts and styles loaded from public CDNs with fixed versions, or self-host them.
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-016 **Tag managers are locked down:** few people can publish tags, and changes are reviewed. A tag manager can inject any script into production.
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-017 **Script sources restricted by CSP:** the Content Security Policy limits which domains scripts can load from (see the **security** section).
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-018 **Third-party scripts don't load on sensitive pages** (login, payment, password reset, admin), or are reviewed for those pages.

### Repository and accounts
- [ ] 🔴 SUP-019 **Secret scanning and push protection are on** for the repository.
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-020 **Branch protection and required reviews** on the default branch, and `CODEOWNERS` for sensitive paths (auth, payments, infra, workflows).
- [ ] 🟡 SUP-021 **Signed commits or verified committers** for maintainers, and 2FA required for the organisation.
- [ ] 🟢 SUP-022 **An SBOM can be generated** (e.g. `npx @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm`) for customers or audits.

<a id="maintainability"></a>

## Maintainability and handover

Load this file for every Full and Enterprise check. AI-built apps often work but can't be maintained, handed to a developer, sold or shown to investors without a rewrite. These checks make sure someone other than the original builder (or their AI) can safely run and change the app. Most items are 🟡 or 🟢: they rarely block a launch, but they decide how expensive every future change is.

### Code health
- [ ] 🟡 MNT-001 **Type safety:** TypeScript `strict` mode (or the language's equivalent), with few `any`, `@ts-ignore` or `eslint-disable` escapes. Each escape has a reason.
- [ ] 🟡 MNT-002 **Linting and formatting run automatically** (ESLint/Biome/Ruff and Prettier, or similar), in CI and on commit.
- [ ] 🟡 MNT-003 **No dead or duplicated code:** unused files, components, routes and exports removed. No copy-pasted versions of the same logic from different AI sessions (see blind spot 16).
- [ ] 🟡 MNT-004 **No giant files or functions:** files over ~500 lines or functions over ~80 lines doing many things are listed for future splitting (list them; don't refactor during the audit).
- [ ] 🟡 MNT-005 **Configuration isn't hard-coded:** URLs, prices, limits, feature switches and email addresses live in config or env vars, not scattered through the code.
- [ ] 🟢 MNT-006 **Consistent structure and naming** that a new developer can guess (where routes, components, server code and tests live).

### Documentation
- [ ] 🔴 MNT-007 **README explains how to run it:** install, required env vars (with an `.env.example` listing every variable and what it's for, no real values), how to run locally, run tests, and deploy.
- [ ] 🟡 MNT-008 **Architecture notes:** a short page or diagram showing the main parts (frontend, API, database, storage, third-party services) and how data flows.
- [ ] 🟡 MNT-009 **Project rules for AI tools** (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules`): stack, conventions, "never do" rules, and how to test, so future AI sessions don't drift.
- [ ] 🟡 MNT-010 **Database schema is documented** through migrations and a short description of the main tables and relationships.
- [ ] 🟢 MNT-011 **Changelog or release notes** for user-visible changes.

### Ownership and handover
- [ ] 🔴 MNT-012 **The business owns every account:** domain, hosting, database, code repository, app store accounts, payment provider, email provider and AI providers are owned by the company (or the client, for agency work), not a freelancer's or employee's personal login. → ask the user.
- [ ] 🔴 MNT-013 **Credentials are in a password manager or vault** that more than one trusted person can access. No credentials only in someone's head or chat history.
- [ ] 🟡 MNT-014 **Licences and third-party terms are listed** for code, assets, fonts, APIs and AI models (see the **legal-privacy** section), so a buyer or investor can check them.
- [ ] 🟡 MNT-015 **Known issues and tech debt are written down,** including shortcuts taken during the build and the latest vibe-check report.
- [ ] 🟢 MNT-016 **Due-diligence pack ready:** architecture notes, security summary, the latest vibe-check report, dependency and licence list, data map, and the policies in the **policies** section.

<a id="ai-features"></a>

## AI and LLM features

Use this file only if the app calls an LLM or AI API (chatbots, generation, agents, RAG, AI image or voice). Mark each item PASS / FAIL / N/A / CAN'T TELL, with evidence.

### Keys and cost

- [ ] 🔴 AIF-001 **AI provider keys stay on the server.** No OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or Replicate key in client code or a public env var. The browser calls your backend, never the provider directly.
- [ ] 🔴 AIF-002 **Per-user limits:** rate limits, daily or monthly quotas, `max_tokens` on every call, and a limit on input size (characters, file size, pages).
- [ ] 🔴 AIF-003 **Spend cap and billing alert** set at the provider (ask the user).
- [ ] 🔴 AIF-004 **Anonymous users can't run up the bill.** Unauthenticated AI endpoints get strict limits or CAPTCHA.
- [ ] 🟡 AIF-005 **Calls are triggered deliberately:** not on every keystroke, render or retry loop. Debounce and cancel in-flight requests.
- [ ] 🟡 AIF-006 **Streaming and long calls** have timeouts and handle user cancellation.
- [ ] 🟢 AIF-007 **Cache** repeated identical prompts where that's safe.

### Prompt injection and output handling

- [ ] 🔴 AIF-008 **LLM output is treated as untrusted input.** It is never rendered as raw HTML (sanitize markdown output), never run as code or SQL, and never used as a URL, file path or shell argument without validation.
- [ ] 🔴 AIF-009 **Prompt injection is assumed.** Text from users, uploaded documents, web pages, emails or RAG sources can contain instructions. The model's permissions must be safe even if it obeys them.
- [ ] 🔴 AIF-010 **Tool and agent permissions are least-privilege.** Tools run with the *end user's* permissions (not admin or service-role). Destructive or costly actions (sending email, payments, deleting, posting) need explicit user confirmation.
- [ ] 🔴 AIF-011 **No data leaks across users.** RAG retrieval and conversation history are filtered by the current user or tenant on the server, not by asking the model.
- [ ] 🟡 AIF-012 **System prompts contain no secrets.** Assume users can extract the system prompt.
- [ ] 🟡 AIF-013 **Structured output is validated** against a schema before use.
- [ ] 🟡 AIF-014 **No exfiltration through rendered markdown.** Images and links in model output can't send data to attacker URLs (restrict image domains or strip external images).

### Privacy, safety and honesty

- [ ] 🔴 AIF-015 **The privacy policy names the AI providers** and says what data is sent to them. Check the provider's data-retention and training terms (opt out of training where possible).
- [ ] 🔴 AIF-016 **No sensitive data sent unnecessarily:** health records, government IDs, passwords and payment data are stripped before prompts.
- [ ] 🟡 AIF-017 **Content moderation** on user prompts and on outputs if the app is public or generates images, so it can't be used to produce harmful content under your brand.
- [ ] 🟡 AIF-018 **AI disclosure.** Users know they're talking to AI. AI-generated content is labelled where laws or platforms require it (EU AI Act transparency rules, app store policies).
- [ ] 🟡 AIF-019 **High-stakes outputs** (health, legal, finance, safety) carry disclaimers and a path to a human.
- [ ] 🟡 AIF-020 **Hallucination handling.** Citations or sources where accuracy matters, and the UI doesn't present guesses as facts.
- [ ] 🟡 AIF-021 **Logs of prompts and outputs** are access-controlled, have a retention limit, and are covered by deletion requests.
- [ ] 🟢 AIF-022 **Evals.** A small set of test prompts (including jailbreak and injection attempts) run before changing models or prompts.
- [ ] 🟢 AIF-023 **Fallback** when the provider is down or rate-limits you, so users see a clear message instead of a hang.

<a id="ai-agents"></a>

## AI agents, tools and MCP servers

Load this file when the app **lets an AI take actions**: an agent that calls tools or APIs, browses, writes to a database, sends messages or spends money, or when the project **is or includes an MCP server, plugin or tool provider** for AI assistants. This is on top of the **ai-features** section, which covers basic LLM use (keys, cost, prompt injection, output handling).

### Tools and permissions
- [ ] 🔴 AGT-001 **Least-privilege tools:** each tool does one specific thing with tightly scoped inputs. No generic "run SQL", "run shell command", "fetch any URL" or "call any API" tools exposed to the model unless sandboxed.
- [ ] 🔴 AGT-002 **Tools act as the end user, not as admin:** every tool call is authorized with the current user's permissions and tenant. The service key or admin token is never what the model uses.
- [ ] 🔴 AGT-003 **Human confirmation for risky actions:** sending email or messages, payments or refunds, deleting data, changing permissions, publishing content and anything irreversible needs explicit user approval in the UI, showing exactly what will happen.
- [ ] 🔴 AGT-004 **Indirect prompt injection is assumed:** content the agent reads (web pages, emails, documents, tickets, database rows, tool results) can contain instructions. The agent's permissions must be safe even if it follows them. Untrusted content is never allowed to choose recipients, URLs or amounts for risky actions without confirmation.
- [ ] 🔴 AGT-005 **No data exfiltration paths:** the agent can't send private data to arbitrary URLs (through fetch tools, rendered images or links, webhooks or email). Outbound destinations are allow-listed.
- [ ] 🟡 AGT-006 **Tool inputs are validated with a schema** on the server, and tool outputs are size-limited and treated as untrusted.
- [ ] 🟡 AGT-007 **Sandboxing for code execution or browsing:** isolated containers or VMs with no access to production secrets or internal networks, plus time, memory and network limits.

### Limits and cost
- [ ] 🔴 AGT-008 **Loop and cost limits:** maximum steps, tool calls, tokens, time and spend per task and per user, with the agent stopping cleanly when a limit is hit.
- [ ] 🟡 AGT-009 **Rate limits per user** on agent runs and expensive tools.
- [ ] 🟡 AGT-010 **Idempotent actions:** retries or repeated agent steps can't double-send, double-charge or create duplicates (idempotency keys on actions).

### Visibility and control
- [ ] 🔴 AGT-011 **Audit log of agent actions:** which user, which tool, inputs (secrets masked), result and time, viewable by the user and admins.
- [ ] 🟡 AGT-012 **Kill switch:** agents or specific tools can be disabled instantly without a deploy.
- [ ] 🟡 AGT-013 **Users can see and undo** what the agent did where possible (drafts before sending, version history).
- [ ] 🟡 AGT-014 **Evaluation set** of normal tasks plus injection and jailbreak attempts, run before changing models, prompts or tools.

### MCP servers, plugins and tool providers
- [ ] 🔴 AGT-015 **Authentication on remote MCP endpoints:** OAuth (with PKCE) or scoped API keys. No unauthenticated remote MCP servers that touch user data. Tokens are scoped per user and revocable.
- [ ] 🔴 AGT-016 **Local MCP servers run with minimal access:** only the folders, commands and network access they need. No shell or filesystem access beyond the stated purpose.
- [ ] 🔴 AGT-017 **Tool descriptions are honest and minimal:** descriptions don't contain instructions aimed at the AI ("always call this tool first", "ignore other tools"), and don't change unexpectedly after users approve them.
- [ ] 🟡 AGT-018 **Destructive tools are clearly marked** (read-only vs write) so clients can ask for confirmation, and they support a dry-run where possible.
- [ ] 🟡 AGT-019 **Data returned to the AI is minimal:** no secrets, internal IDs or other users' data in tool results. Large results are paginated.
- [ ] 🟡 AGT-020 **Published packages are signed and pinned:** users install a known version, and updates are reviewed (a malicious update to a tool server reaches every user).

<a id="kids-education"></a>

## Children, students and education

Load this file when anyone under 18 can use the app, or when it serves schools, colleges or students. Children's data carries the strictest obligations, and the biggest consequences if it leaks. Flag every legal item for a lawyer, and for the institution if a school, college or government body runs the program.

**Laws to name, depending on where users are:** India DPDP Act (under 18 = child: verifiable parental consent, no tracking, no behavioural monitoring, no targeted ads). US COPPA (under 13), FERPA (school records), and state student-privacy laws. EU/UK GDPR (age of consent 13–16 by country) and the UK Age-Appropriate Design Code.

### Age and consent
- [ ] 🔴 KID-001 **The age or school level is known.** The app can tell whether a user is a minor (date of birth, class or grade, or the institution says so).
- [ ] 🔴 KID-002 **Verifiable parental or guardian consent** before collecting a minor's personal data, where the law requires it. **A checkbox the child ticks is not verifiable consent.** The decision on the method belongs to the institution and its lawyer; flag it rather than inventing one.
- [ ] 🔴 KID-003 **Consent is recorded:** who consented, for which child, when, how, and which version of the notice.
- [ ] 🟡 KID-004 **Consent can be withdrawn**, and withdrawing it triggers deletion.
- [ ] 🟡 KID-005 **The notice for children and parents** uses plain language, in the users' languages.

### Data minimization and retention
- [ ] 🔴 KID-006 **Only necessary data is collected.** No extra fields "for later". Every field in the data map has a purpose.
- [ ] 🔴 KID-007 **Retention limits exist and are enforced:** photos, documents and records of minors are deleted or anonymized on a schedule (e.g. X days after the event or term). **Keeping minors' data forever is a 🔴.**
- [ ] 🔴 KID-008 **Photos and media:** EXIF and GPS metadata is stripped unless needed and disclosed. Faces of minors aren't public. Access to media is logged.
- [ ] 🟡 KID-009 **Pseudonymization is described accurately:** hashed or coded IDs and phone numbers are described honestly (hashes of phone numbers can often be reversed by brute force; don't claim "cannot be reversed").

### Tracking, ads and profiling
- [ ] 🔴 KID-010 **No third-party trackers, ad pixels or session replay** on pages minors use.
- [ ] 🔴 KID-011 **No targeted advertising or behavioural profiling** of minors.
- [ ] 🟡 KID-012 **Third-party embeds and fonts** (YouTube, Google Fonts, chat widgets) are disclosed. Self-host where possible.

### Access and safety
- [ ] 🔴 KID-013 **Least-privilege staff access.** Teachers and staff see only their own students. Admin access is limited, logged and reviewed.
- [ ] 🔴 KID-014 **Students' personal details are never returned** by any public page, API, export or search.
- [ ] 🟡 KID-015 **No public profiles or open messaging** between adults and minors unless that's the product's purpose, and then with moderation and reporting.
- [ ] 🟡 KID-016 **Exports** (CSV, PDF) containing student data are restricted, logged and watermarked where possible.

### Institutions and government programs
- [ ] 🟡 KID-017 **Roles are clear:** who is the data fiduciary or controller (school, district, department), and who is the processor (you). A written agreement exists or is planned.
- [ ] 🟡 KID-018 **Hosting and certification requirements asked about** (e.g. Indian government programs may need MeitY-empanelled hosting, a CERT-In-empanelled or STQC security audit, and GIGW website compliance). → ask the user.
- [ ] 🟡 KID-019 **A named grievance officer or contact** is in the privacy policy, with a response timeline.
- [ ] 🟡 KID-020 **Breach plan for student data:** who notifies the institution, parents and regulator, and how fast.

<a id="health"></a>

## Health, medical, wellness and fitness

Load this file when the app collects health, medical, mental-health, fitness, fertility or biometric data, or gives health advice. Laws to flag for a lawyer: US HIPAA (if you work with covered entities) and state health-data laws (e.g. Washington's My Health My Data Act). EU/UK GDPR, where health data is a "special category" that needs explicit consent. India DPDP Act, plus telemedicine and Digital Health (ABDM) rules where relevant.

- [ ] 🔴 HLT-001 **Explicit, separate consent** for health data, not bundled into the terms.
- [ ] 🔴 HLT-002 **No health data sent to analytics, ad pixels, session replay or marketing tools** (including URL paths and event names that reveal conditions).
- [ ] 🔴 HLT-003 **Encryption at rest and in transit.** Field-level encryption for diagnoses, notes and documents.
- [ ] 🔴 HLT-004 **Strict access control** with audit logs on every read of health records.
- [ ] 🔴 HLT-005 **Medical disclaimer** and an emergency path ("If this is an emergency, call …") wherever advice or AI answers appear.
- [ ] 🔴 HLT-006 **AI features** don't diagnose or prescribe unless the product is approved for that. Output is labelled as AI, with a route to a human professional.
- [ ] 🟡 HLT-007 **A BAA or DPA** with every vendor that touches health data (hosting, email, AI provider). Many default plans don't allow health data.
- [ ] 🟡 HLT-008 **Retention and deletion** rules for health records, including backups and AI provider logs.
- [ ] 🟡 HLT-009 **Notifications** (push, email, SMS) don't reveal health details on lock screens or in subject lines.
- [ ] 🟡 HLT-010 **Regulatory status checked:** does the feature make the app a medical device or software as a medical device (CDSCO in India, FDA in the US, MDR in the EU)? → lawyer.

<a id="fintech"></a>

## Payments, wallets and financial features

Load this file when the app takes payments, holds balances, pays out to users, lends, invests, or handles financial data. Also check the payments items in the **legal-privacy** section and the Stripe/Razorpay section of the **platforms** section.

### Payments
- [ ] 🔴 FIN-001 **No card numbers anywhere in your systems:** logs, DB, analytics, support tools and error tracking. (Hosted checkout is checked in the **legal-privacy** section.)
- [ ] 🔴 FIN-002 **Amounts, currency and tax** are calculated on the server.
- [ ] 🔴 FIN-003 **Webhooks are verified and idempotent.** Entitlements are granted and revoked only from verified events (paid, refunded, disputed, cancelled, failed).
- [ ] 🔴 FIN-004 **Test and live modes are separate.** Failure, refund, dispute and cancel flows were rehearsed in test mode.
- [ ] 🟡 FIN-005 **Reconciliation:** a daily check that your records match the processor's (missed webhooks happen).
- [ ] 🟡 FIN-006 **Invoices and receipts** meet local rules (e.g. GST invoices in India, VAT in the EU). → accountant.
- [ ] 🟡 FIN-007 **Recurring payments** follow local mandate rules (e.g. RBI e-mandate and pre-debit notifications in India).

### Money movement and balances
- [ ] 🔴 FIN-008 **A ledger, not a balance column:** balances come from immutable, double-entry transactions. No `UPDATE balance = …` without a transaction record.
- [ ] 🔴 FIN-009 **Atomic transfers,** with constraints that prevent negative balances and double spends (see the **fixes** section, race conditions).
- [ ] 🔴 FIN-010 **Payouts** need verified identity and bank details, with limits, delays for new accounts, and manual review for unusual amounts.
- [ ] 🟡 FIN-011 **Fraud controls:** velocity limits, device and IP signals, card-testing protection on checkout, alerts for spikes in refunds or disputes.

### Regulation (flag for a lawyer; don't decide)
- [ ] 🔴 FIN-012 **Licensing check:** holding customer funds, wallets, lending, investment advice, crypto, or cross-border transfers may need a licence or a regulated partner (RBI PA/PPI rules in India, money transmitter licences in the US, EMI in the EU). → lawyer.
- [ ] 🟡 FIN-013 **KYC/AML** obligations if you onboard payees or hold funds.
- [ ] 🟡 FIN-014 **Financial advice disclaimers,** and no guaranteed-return claims.
- [ ] 🟡 FIN-015 **Data retention** for financial records follows the legal minimums (often 5–8 years), while other personal data is still minimized.

<a id="policies"></a>

## Policy pack: what the app must publish

Check which documents exist, whether they're linked where users need them, and whether **each one matches the data map and features from Step 2**. A generic template that doesn't match the app is a FAIL. Drafting is allowed only on request and only from the real data map; mark drafts "DRAFT – needs legal review" and add them to the "Needs a lawyer" list.

| Document | Needed when | Must include | Link it from |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🔴 **Privacy policy** | Always, if any personal data is collected | Each data type and its purpose, legal basis, processors and third parties (hosting, email, analytics, AI, fonts/CDNs), storage location and region, retention, user rights and how to use them, children's data (if any), a contact or grievance officer, an effective date | Footer, signup, every form that collects data |
| 🔴 **Terms of service** | Always | Who can use it, acceptable use, accounts, payments (if any), IP, termination, disclaimers, liability limit, governing law, contact | Footer, signup |
| 🔴 **Cookie notice and consent** | Non-essential cookies or trackers, with EU/UK users (and good practice everywhere) | Each cookie and tracker with its purpose and duration, plus a consent banner that blocks non-essential cookies until consent | Footer and the banner |
| 🔴 **Refund and cancellation policy** | The app charges money | How to cancel, refund rules, trial terms, processing times | Pricing, checkout, footer |
| 🔴 **Parental consent notice** | Minors (see the **kids-education** section) | What is collected about the child, why, retention, rights, how to withdraw consent | The consent flow |
| 🟡 **Acceptable use policy** | User-generated content, uploads or messaging | Prohibited content and behaviour, enforcement, how to report | Terms, report flow |
| 🟡 **Content and copyright takedown** | Users upload content | A contact for copyright and abuse reports, the process and timelines | Footer |
| 🟡 **AI disclosure** | AI features | What's AI-generated, its limits, which providers, whether data is used for training | Near the AI feature, privacy policy |
| 🟡 **Disclaimer** | Health, finance, legal, safety or fitness advice | "Not professional advice", plus when to see a professional | Near the advice |
| 🟡 **Accessibility statement** | Public, government or EU-market apps | Standard targeted (WCAG 2.2 AA), known gaps, contact | Footer |
| 🟡 **Data retention schedule** | Personal data is kept | How long each data type is kept and how it's deleted | Privacy policy, or internal |
| 🟡 **Subprocessor list** | B2B customers | Every vendor that processes customer data, with its location | Trust or legal page |
| 🟡 **Data processing agreement (DPA)** | B2B customers process personal data through you | Roles, security measures, subprocessors, breach notice, deletion | Available on request |
| 🟡 **`security.txt` and a vulnerability disclosure policy** | Public apps | A contact for security reports (`/.well-known/security.txt`) | Footer, or the well-known path |
| 🟡 **Incident response plan** | Personal data or paid users | Who does what, notification timelines (e.g. GDPR 72h, CERT-In 6h in India), contacts | Internal |
| 🟢 **Status page and SLA** | Paid or B2B | Uptime target, credits if any, how incidents are communicated | Footer, contracts |

### Checks
- [ ] 🔴 POL-001 **Required documents exist:** each one is reachable without logging in and linked where users need it.
- [ ] 🔴 POL-002 **Documents match the app today,** including recently added fields and features (compare against the data map).
- [ ] 🔴 POL-003 **No overstated claims:** ("cannot be reversed", "fully anonymous", "bank-grade", "100% secure", "compliant" without proof).
- [ ] 🟡 POL-004 **Dated and versioned:** each document has an effective date and a version history, and users are told about material changes.
- [ ] 🟡 POL-005 **In the users' languages,** and the translations match.
- [ ] 🟡 POL-006 **Contact details work** (the email inbox is monitored).

<a id="enterprise"></a>

## Enterprise and government readiness

Load this file at the Enterprise level: when selling to companies or government, or handling regulated data. This is what security reviews, procurement teams and auditors ask for. Many items are documents and processes, not code: mark them CAN'T TELL and ask the user.

### Identity and access
- [ ] 🔴 ENT-001 **SSO** (SAML or OIDC) for customer orgs, with **SCIM** or just-in-time provisioning and deprovisioning.
- [ ] 🔴 ENT-002 **Role-based access** with org-level admins. Customer admins can manage their own users.
- [ ] 🔴 ENT-003 **MFA required** for your own admin and production access (cloud, GitHub, DB, domain registrar, email).
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-004 **Access reviews** every quarter. Leavers are removed the same day. Shared accounts are avoided.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-005 **Break-glass** emergency access is documented and logged.

### Audit and integrity
- [ ] 🔴 ENT-006 **Audit logs** for security-relevant events (logins, permission changes, exports, deletions, admin actions), exportable to the customer.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-007 **Tamper evidence:** logs are append-only, or copied somewhere admins of the main system can't change them (a separate account, object lock, hash chaining). Be accurate about what "tamper-proof" means.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-008 **Change management:** PR review required, protected branches, deploys traceable to commits, separation of duties for production changes.

### Data
- [ ] 🔴 ENT-009 **Data residency** known and matching what customers or regulations require (e.g. India-only hosting for some government work).
- [ ] 🔴 ENT-010 **Encryption** at rest and in transit, with key management documented.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-011 **Tenant isolation** proven by tests: no cross-tenant reads in APIs, search, exports, caches or AI features.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-012 **Customer data export and deletion** at contract end, with a timeline.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-013 **Backups:** encrypted and off-site, with documented RPO and RTO targets (how much data you could lose, how long recovery takes), and **restore tested** with a date recorded.

### Security program
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-014 **Threat model** for the main flows and data.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-015 **Third-party penetration test** within the last 12 months, with findings fixed. Government work may need a CERT-In-empanelled auditor or STQC.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-016 **Vulnerability management:** dependency scanning in CI, an SLA for patching criticals, `security.txt`.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-017 **SBOM** (software bill of materials) can be generated (e.g. `npx @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm`).
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-018 **Secrets management:** a vault or platform secrets, rotation schedule, no shared credentials.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-019 **Incident response plan** with notification timelines, tested with a tabletop exercise.
- [ ] 🟢 ENT-020 **SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001 readiness.** Policies exist (access, change, incident, vendor, BCP). A compliance tool (Vanta, Drata, Sprinto) helps when a certification is needed.

### Reliability and operations
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-021 **SLOs and an SLA**, uptime monitoring, a public status page, and incident communication.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-022 **Disaster recovery and business continuity plan:** a cloud region failure, a lost account, a key person unavailable.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-023 **Bus factor and ownership:** at least two people can access and operate production. The domain, cloud, code and DB are owned by the company, not a personal account. No production on a personal-name domain.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-024 **Environments:** dev, staging and production are isolated, with no production data in lower environments (or it's masked).

### Procurement and compliance documents
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-025 **Security questionnaire answers** ready (CAIQ, SIG-lite, or the customer's own).
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-026 **Trust page:** security overview, subprocessors, DPA, status, contact.
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-027 **Accessibility conformance report** (VPAT or WCAG report). Government sites may need GIGW (India), Section 508 (US) or EN 301 549 (EU).
- [ ] 🟡 ENT-028 **Insurance** (cyber, professional liability) if contracts require it. → ask the user.

<a id="mobile"></a>

## Mobile apps (iOS and Android)

Load this file when the project contains a mobile app: native iOS or Android, React Native, Expo, Capacitor, Ionic, Flutter or a store-published PWA wrapper. App store rejections and mobile-only security problems are among the most common launch blockers. Check `Info.plist`, `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, `AndroidManifest.xml`, `app.json`/`app.config.*`, `capacitor.config.*`, `build.gradle`, and the native project folders.

### App store requirements
- [ ] 🔴 MOB-001 **Account deletion inside the app** if the app lets people create accounts (Apple and Google both require it). The flow deletes server data too, not just the local session.
- [ ] 🔴 MOB-002 **Permission purpose strings for every permission the app can trigger:** `NSCameraUsageDescription`, `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription`, `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`, `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` and so on, in clear words. A missing string makes iOS **crash** the app when that feature is used (for example "Take Photo" in a file picker on iPad).
- [ ] 🔴 MOB-003 **Privacy labels match reality:** App Store privacy "nutrition labels" and the Google Play Data safety form list every data type collected, including by SDKs (analytics, crash reporting, ads, AI, auth).
- [ ] 🔴 MOB-004 **Apple privacy manifest** (`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`) for the app, declaring required-reason APIs and tracking domains, and third-party SDKs that ship their own manifests are up to date.
- [ ] 🔴 MOB-005 **Digital goods use in-app purchase** where the store rules require it, and receipts or purchase tokens are **verified on the server**, never trusted from the device.
- [ ] 🔴 MOB-006 **Tracking permission:** if the app tracks users across other companies' apps or websites (ad SDKs, cross-app attribution), it asks with App Tracking Transparency on iOS before tracking.
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-007 **Sign in with Apple** is offered on iOS where Apple's rules require it (when other third-party social logins are offered).
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-008 **Target and minimum SDK versions** meet Google Play's current target API requirement and Apple's current SDK requirement.
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-009 **Store listing is honest:** screenshots, description, age rating and content questionnaire match the app (e.g. user chat or AI features change the rating). A support URL and privacy policy URL work.
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-010 **Review notes and a demo account** are prepared for app review if features need sign-in.

### Mobile security
- [ ] 🔴 MOB-011 **No secrets in the app bundle:** API secret keys, service-role keys and private tokens aren't in the JS bundle, `.env` files compiled into the app, `Info.plist`, `strings.xml` or `google-services.json` beyond the public config. Anything shipped in an app can be extracted.
- [ ] 🔴 MOB-012 **Tokens stored securely:** session and refresh tokens live in Keychain/Keystore (e.g. `expo-secure-store`, `@capacitor/preferences` with secure storage, `flutter_secure_storage`), not AsyncStorage, `localStorage` or plain files.
- [ ] 🔴 MOB-013 **HTTPS only:** no `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` / `usesCleartextTraffic="true"` in production builds, except narrowly for documented local development.
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-014 **Deep links and universal/app links are verified** (`apple-app-site-association`, `assetlinks.json`), and parameters from links are validated before use (no account actions straight from a link).
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-015 **WebViews are locked down:** no JavaScript bridges exposed to remote content, only trusted domains loaded, and file access disabled unless needed.
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-016 **Debug features are off in release builds:** no dev menus, debug logs with personal data, test endpoints or `debuggable=true`.
- [ ] 🟢 MOB-017 **Screenshots and app switcher** hide sensitive screens (payment, health, private messages) where appropriate.

### Reliability and quality
- [ ] 🔴 MOB-018 **Crash and error reporting** (Sentry, Crashlytics or similar) in release builds, with personal data scrubbed.
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-019 **Forced update path:** the app can tell users to update when an old version is no longer supported, and the API stays backwards-compatible with versions still in use.
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-020 **Offline and poor network:** the app shows clear states, doesn't lose drafts, and retries safely (no double payments).
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-021 **Permissions are requested in context** (when the feature is first used), with a friendly explanation and a way forward if refused.
- [ ] 🟡 MOB-022 **Tested on real devices:** small and large phones, tablets (iPad split view and rotation), the oldest supported OS version, and dark mode.
- [ ] 🟢 MOB-023 **App size and startup time** are reasonable, and large assets load on demand.
- [ ] 🟢 MOB-024 **Push notifications** ask permission in context, can be turned off in settings, and don't show sensitive content on the lock screen.

<a id="community"></a>

## Community, chat and marketplaces

Load this file when users can post content others see, message each other, join groups, follow each other, review things, or buy and sell from each other. These apps carry abuse, safety and legal duties that ordinary apps don't. Flag legal judgement calls for a lawyer.

### Safety tools
- [ ] 🔴 COM-001 **Report button** on every piece of user content, profile and message, with a reason and an acknowledgement to the reporter.
- [ ] 🔴 COM-002 **Block and mute:** users can block others, and blocking stops messages, mentions, follows and seeing each other's content.
- [ ] 🔴 COM-003 **Moderation queue:** staff can review reports, remove content, warn, suspend and ban, with an audit log of every action and the reason.
- [ ] 🔴 COM-004 **Automatic filtering** of obvious abuse: slurs, spam links, scams, and sexual or violent content in text and images (e.g. a moderation API or model), with stricter defaults where minors are present.
- [ ] 🔴 COM-005 **Minors and adults:** if under-18s can use the app, check who can message them, whether adults can find or contact minors, and whether there's age-appropriate default privacy (see the **kids-education** section).
- [ ] 🟡 COM-006 **Appeals:** users told why content was removed or an account suspended, with a way to appeal.
- [ ] 🟡 COM-007 **New-account limits:** rate limits on posts, messages, invites and links for new or unverified accounts, to slow spam and raids.
- [ ] 🟡 COM-008 **Images and files:** uploads are scanned or moderated before others see them, and EXIF/GPS metadata is stripped (see the **security** section).

### Chat and real-time
- [ ] 🔴 COM-009 **WebSocket and real-time channels check authorization** on connect **and** on every subscribe or message: users can only join rooms, channels and conversations they belong to (Supabase Realtime, Firebase, Pusher, Socket.IO, Ably).
- [ ] 🔴 COM-010 **Message rate limits and size limits** per user and per room.
- [ ] 🟡 COM-011 **Message deletion and retention:** users can delete their messages, deleted messages are really removed, and the retention period is stated in the privacy policy.
- [ ] 🟡 COM-012 **Links in messages** are shown safely (no auto-loading of untrusted previews from the server without SSRF protection).

### Legal duties (flag for a lawyer)
- [ ] 🔴 COM-013 **Notice and takedown:** a way for anyone (not just users) to report illegal content or copyright infringement, with a contact address and response timeline. → lawyer.
- [ ] 🔴 COM-014 **Child sexual abuse material:** a process to remove and report it to the authorities as the law requires (e.g. NCMEC in the US). Never just delete silently. → lawyer.
- [ ] 🟡 COM-015 **Platform rules by region:** EU Digital Services Act (notice-and-action, statements of reasons, transparency), UK Online Safety Act (risk assessments, reporting, child safety), India IT Rules (grievance officer, takedown timelines). → lawyer.
- [ ] 🟡 COM-016 **Community guidelines and terms** state what's not allowed and what happens, and they're linked at sign-up and in the report flow.

### Marketplaces and paid creators
- [ ] 🔴 COM-017 **Seller or creator verification** before payouts (identity and bank details), with payout holds for new accounts and manual review of unusual amounts (see the **fintech** section).
- [ ] 🔴 COM-018 **Money flows checked by a lawyer:** if users pay other users, or credits can be turned into money, check whether the business needs a payments licence or a regulated partner. → lawyer.
- [ ] 🟡 COM-019 **Disputes and refunds** between buyers and sellers have a clear process and timeline.
- [ ] 🟡 COM-020 **Fake reviews and ratings:** only real buyers or users can review, and incentivised reviews are labelled.
- [ ] 🟡 COM-021 **Prohibited items and services** are listed and enforced (weapons, drugs, counterfeit goods, adult services where not allowed).
- [ ] 🟢 COM-022 **Seller information** shown to buyers where e-commerce rules require it (e.g. EU, India).

<a id="cloud-infra"></a>

## Cloud infrastructure (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Kubernetes)

Load this file when the app runs on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, DigitalOcean, Hetzner or similar, or uses Kubernetes, Terraform, Pulumi, CloudFormation or Docker Compose in production. Platform apps (Vercel, Netlify, Supabase, Firebase, Cloudflare) are covered in the **platforms** section. Read the IaC files and deployment configs. If the user has the cloud CLI logged in, run **read-only** commands only (`aws s3api get-bucket-policy-status`, `gcloud … describe`, `az … show`), never anything that changes resources.

### Storage
- [ ] 🔴 CLD-001 **No public buckets with private data:** S3 Block Public Access on (account and bucket), GCS uniform access without `allUsers`/`allAuthenticatedUsers`, Azure containers not set to public access. Public assets live in a separate, clearly public bucket.
- [ ] 🔴 CLD-002 **Cloud storage and disks encrypted** (buckets, databases, disks and snapshots) (default encryption on, customer-managed keys for sensitive data if required).
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-003 **Versioning and lifecycle rules** on important buckets, so deleted or overwritten files can be recovered and old data expires on schedule.
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-004 **Signed URLs** with short expiry for private files, never long-lived public links.

### Identity and access (IAM)
- [ ] 🔴 CLD-005 **No wildcard permissions** for app roles (`"Action": "*"`, `"Resource": "*"`, Owner/Editor roles for service accounts).
- [ ] 🔴 CLD-006 **No long-lived access keys in code or CI:** use instance roles, workload identity or OIDC for CI. Old keys are rotated or deleted.
- [ ] 🔴 CLD-007 **Root/owner account locked down:** MFA on, no access keys, used only for break-glass. Billing alerts set.
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-008 **Separate accounts or projects** for production and non-production.
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-009 **Cloud audit logs on** (CloudTrail, Cloud Audit Logs, Azure Activity Log) and kept for at least 90 days.

### Network
- [ ] 🔴 CLD-010 **Databases, caches and admin ports aren't open to the internet:** no `0.0.0.0/0` on 5432, 3306, 27017, 6379, 9200, 22 or RDP. Databases are in private subnets.
- [ ] 🔴 CLD-011 **TLS on every public endpoint** (load balancers, API gateways, CDNs), with HTTP redirected and old TLS versions disabled.
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-012 **SSH access** by key only (or through a bastion or session manager), no password login, no root login.
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-013 **WAF or rate limiting** at the edge for public APIs and login.

### Kubernetes and containers
- [ ] 🔴 CLD-014 **Secrets aren't in images or plain manifests:** use Kubernetes Secrets with encryption at rest, or an external secret manager. `docker history` shows no secrets.
- [ ] 🔴 CLD-015 **Containers don't run as root or privileged** unless required (`runAsNonRoot`, no `privileged: true`, read-only root filesystem where possible).
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-016 **Resource requests and limits** set, so one service can't starve others.
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-017 **Images from trusted registries,** pinned by digest or version (not `latest`), and scanned for vulnerabilities.
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-018 **The Kubernetes API and dashboards aren't public,** and RBAC follows least privilege.

### Infrastructure as Code
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-019 **IaC scanned** for misconfigurations (e.g. `tfsec`, `checkov`, `trivy config`), and state files (Terraform state) stored privately and encrypted, since they contain secrets.
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-020 **Changes go through review and CI,** not manual console edits (drift is detected).
- [ ] 🟡 CLD-021 **Backups and snapshots are automatic** for databases and volumes, and a restore has been tested (see the **devops** section).
- [ ] 🟢 CLD-022 **Cost controls:** budgets and alerts, auto-scaling limits, and no forgotten resources (unused instances, load balancers, IPs, snapshots).

<a id="desktop-extensions"></a>

## Desktop apps and browser extensions

Load this file when the project is an Electron, Tauri or other desktop app, or a browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari). These run with more power on the user's computer than a website does, so mistakes are more dangerous.

### Electron and Tauri
- [ ] 🔴 DSK-001 **Electron isolation on:** `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true` for every window. Renderer code can't call Node APIs directly.
- [ ] 🔴 DSK-002 **Safe preload bridge:** `contextBridge` exposes only specific, validated functions, never `ipcRenderer` itself or generic "run this command" or "read this file" functions.
- [ ] 🔴 DSK-003 **No remote content with privileges:** the app doesn't load remote websites in privileged windows. External links open in the system browser (`shell.openExternal` with an allow-list of protocols), and navigation and new windows are restricted.
- [ ] 🔴 DSK-004 **Code signing and notarization:** builds are signed (Apple Developer ID + notarization on macOS, Authenticode on Windows), so users aren't trained to bypass security warnings.
- [ ] 🔴 DSK-005 **Secure auto-update:** updates come over HTTPS from a trusted source and are signature-checked (electron-updater with signing, Tauri updater with public key).
- [ ] 🟡 DSK-006 **Tauri allow-lists:** only the APIs, file paths and shell commands the app needs are enabled in the Tauri config or capabilities.
- [ ] 🟡 DSK-007 **Content Security Policy** set for app windows, and no `eval` or remote scripts.
- [ ] 🟡 DSK-008 **Local data protection:** tokens in the OS keychain (`keytar`, `safeStorage`, Tauri stronghold or keyring), not plain files. Local databases with sensitive data are encrypted.
- [ ] 🟡 DSK-009 **Electron is kept up to date** (old Chromium versions carry known vulnerabilities).
- [ ] 🟢 DSK-010 **Crash reporting and a way to collect logs** with the user's consent.

### Browser extensions
- [ ] 🔴 DSK-011 **Minimal permissions:** only the `permissions` and `host_permissions` the extension really needs. No `<all_urls>` unless essential (prefer `activeTab` and optional permissions requested in context).
- [ ] 🔴 DSK-012 **Manifest V3** for Chrome and Edge, with no remotely hosted code (all scripts packaged), as store policies require.
- [ ] 🔴 DSK-013 **Content scripts don't trust the page:** messages from web pages (`window.postMessage`) are validated, and page data is never passed to `eval`, `innerHTML` or privileged APIs without checking the sender and content.
- [ ] 🔴 DSK-014 **Data handling matches the store disclosure:** the Chrome Web Store privacy practices form, Firefox data collection disclosure and the privacy policy describe exactly what's collected (browsing history, page content), and limited-use rules are followed.
- [ ] 🟡 DSK-015 **Secrets aren't in the extension package:** API keys used by the extension are public-safe or go through your server.
- [ ] 🟡 DSK-016 **External messaging restricted:** `externally_connectable` lists only your own domains, if used.
- [ ] 🟡 DSK-017 **Store listing is accurate:** single, clear purpose, honest screenshots and description, a support contact.
- [ ] 🟢 DSK-018 **Update and rollback plan:** store review can delay fixes, so risky features are behind server-side flags.

<a id="i18n"></a>

## Internationalisation and localisation

Load this file when the app supports more than one language or region, sells to several countries, or targets users whose language isn't English. Translation gaps and wrong formats look broken to users, and in some places (e.g. Quebec) missing language versions are a legal problem (see the **lawsuits** section).

### Language
- [ ] 🔴 LOC-001 **No missing translations:** every visible string in each supported language, including errors, emails, notifications, buttons, empty states, legal pages and app store listings. No raw keys like `checkout.button.pay` or mixed languages on one screen.
- [ ] 🔴 LOC-002 **Legal and consent text in each language users get,** and the translations say the same thing as the original (privacy policy, terms, consent banner, parental consent).
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-003 **Strings aren't hard-coded** in components. They come from translation files, so new languages can be added.
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-004 **Plurals and grammar handled properly** (ICU message format or the library's plural rules), not `count + " items"`.
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-005 **Language selection:** detected sensibly (browser or device language), changeable by the user, remembered, and the `lang` attribute is set on pages for screen readers and SEO.
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-006 **Machine-translated text reviewed** by a fluent speaker for key flows (sign-up, payment, legal).
- [ ] 🟢 LOC-007 **SEO for languages:** separate URLs per language and `hreflang` tags (see the **launch-ux** section).

### Layout and text
- [ ] 🔴 LOC-008 **Scripts render correctly:** non-Latin scripts (Hindi, Tamil, Arabic, Chinese and others) display with suitable fonts, with no boxes (tofu) or broken characters in UI, PDFs, emails and exports.
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-009 **Right-to-left languages** (Arabic, Hebrew, Urdu) mirror the layout correctly if supported (`dir="rtl"`, logical CSS properties).
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-010 **Longer text fits:** layouts handle translations that are 30–50% longer than English (German, Tamil) without overflow or cut-off buttons.
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-011 **Search, sorting and validation** work for non-English text (accents, case, local sorting order, names that don't fit "first name / last name").

### Formats and regional rules
- [ ] 🔴 LOC-012 **Prices and currencies are right:** the correct currency and symbol, local number format (e.g. 1,00,000 in India and 100.000,00 in Germany), and taxes shown the way each region expects (prices with or without VAT/GST).
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-013 **Dates, times and time zones** are shown in the user's format and time zone (see the **functional-qa** section).
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-014 **Phone numbers and addresses** accept international formats (E.164 for phones), with no US-only fields like "State" or "ZIP" made mandatory for everyone.
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-015 **Units** (metric or imperial, sizes) suit the region if the app shows them.
- [ ] 🟡 LOC-016 **Payment methods** fit each region (UPI in India, iDEAL in the Netherlands, local cards), if the app sells there.
- [ ] 🟢 LOC-017 **Regional content and features** that are restricted or different per country (age limits, banned products, data residency) are handled.

Use this structure. Keep it skimmable. Plain words first, technical details second.


### Writing tips

- Order blockers by severity: data leaks and account takeover first, then money loss, then legal, then outages.
- One finding per real problem. Group repeats (for example, "12 routes are missing ownership checks", with all 12 listed).
- For dependency findings, give the advisory ID, installed version and fixed version.
- Never print a full secret.
- Only ✅ Confirmed and 🔎 Likely findings go in Blockers or Fix before scale. ❓ items are questions.
- Legal and policy statements cite the skill module or a URL opened in this run, never general memory. Show its first 4 characters and its location.
- If something is fine, don't invent a problem to look thorough.

### Score card, badge and footer

These go at the very end of the saved report **and** the chat summary.

#### Score card (always)
One line, in a `text` code block, so it screenshots cleanly:

`vibe-check: <🟢 SHIP | 🟡 SHIP AFTER FIXES | 🔴 DO NOT SHIP> · <passed>/<applicable> checks · <n> blockers · <Quick check|Full check|Enterprise check> · <D Mon YYYY>`

- `passed / applicable` counts only items marked PASS out of items that weren't N/A. CAN'T TELL counts as not passed.
- **Never include** findings, secrets, private URLs, file paths, or the app name, unless the user asks for the app name. The card is meant to be shared publicly.
- If the score improved since the last report in `.vibe-check/reports/`, add the change: `· was 🔴 71/118`. Before-and-after posts are the most shared.

#### Badge (only for 🟢 SHIP on a Full or Enterprise check)
Offer this snippet for the user's README. **Don't add it yourself** unless the user says yes (scope guard):

```markdown
[![vibe-checked](https://img.shields.io/badge/vibe--checked-%E2%9C%85%20SHIP%20<passed>%2F<applicable>-brightgreen)](https://github.com/vikneshchandrasekaran21/Vibe-check)
```

Replace `<passed>` and `<applicable>` with the numbers (`%2F` is the slash).

#### Star request (only for 🟢, once)
One line, after the badge: *"If vibe-check helped, a ⭐ on https://github.com/vikneshchandrasekaran21/Vibe-check helps others find it."* Don't repeat it in the same session, and never show it for 🟡 or 🔴.

#### Footer (always, removable)
The last line of the saved report: `<sub>Checked with vibe-check v<installed> · github.com/vikneshchandrasekaran21/Vibe-check · update: npx skills update</sub>`. Leave it out if the user has asked for no footer (or `.vibe-check/config` contains `footer: false`). Never add it to the user's app, pages or code, only to the report.

<a id="fixes"></a>

## Fix playbook

Use these patterns when fixing findings (Step 5), and for the **Fix** and **Prompt to fix it** lines in the report. Adapt each one to the project's stack and the versions actually installed. Check the official docs for that version before writing code.

### How to fix (applies to every recipe)

1. **Prove the bug first.** Write a failing test, or a reproducible request (curl, script), that shows the problem.
2. **Make the smallest correct change, and keep the product as it is.** Don't change the design, features, flows or copy (see *Scope guard* in SKILL.md). If the fix must add something users will see, get approval and build it with the project's existing components and styles. Fix the root cause in one place (a shared helper, a policy or a middleware) rather than patching every caller differently.
3. **Don't add dependencies casually.** Use what the project already has. If you need a new package, check it's real, maintained and widely used, and tell the user.
4. **Verify.** The test from step 1 now passes, the other tests still pass, and the original check from the audit is re-run and marked PASS with new evidence.
5. **One issue per commit**, with a message that says what was wrong and how it was fixed.
6. **If the fix needs the user** (rotating a key in a dashboard, changing DNS, a legal decision), stop and give them exact step-by-step instructions instead of guessing.

---

### Access control

#### Missing authorization / IDOR
**Pattern:** every read or write of a record is scoped to the current user or tenant on the server. Return **404** (not 403) for records the user doesn't own, so IDs can't be discovered.
```ts
// before: db.invoice.findUnique({ where: { id } })
const invoice = await db.invoice.findFirst({ where: { id, userId: session.user.id } });
if (!invoice) return new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });
```
- Put the check in one helper (`requireOwner`, `getUserScopedQuery`) and use it everywhere. Search for every other query on the same table.
- Admin-only routes call a server-side `requireRole("admin")`. Hiding a button is not access control.
- **Test:** create users A and B. A requests B's record by ID and gets 404, for read, update and delete.

#### Supabase RLS
```sql
alter table public.notes enable row level security;

create policy "own rows: select" on public.notes for select using (auth.uid() = user_id);
create policy "own rows: insert" on public.notes for insert with check (auth.uid() = user_id);
create policy "own rows: update" on public.notes for update using (auth.uid() = user_id) with check (auth.uid() = user_id);
create policy "own rows: delete" on public.notes for delete using (auth.uid() = user_id);
```
- Write it as a migration (`supabase migration new rls_notes`), not in the dashboard.
- For teams, check membership: `using (exists (select 1 from members m where m.org_id = notes.org_id and m.user_id = auth.uid()))`.
- Remove any `using (true)` policy on user data. Move code that needs `service_role` into a server route or edge function.
- Storage: make the bucket private and add policies on `storage.objects` that check `auth.uid()` against the path or owner.
- **Test:** with the anon key and user B's session, try to read user A's rows. You should get an empty result.

#### Firebase rules
```
match /notes/{noteId} {
  allow read, delete: if request.auth != null && resource.data.ownerId == request.auth.uid;
  allow create: if request.auth != null && request.resource.data.ownerId == request.auth.uid
                && request.resource.data.keys().hasOnly(['ownerId','title','body','createdAt']);
  allow update: if request.auth != null && resource.data.ownerId == request.auth.uid
                && request.resource.data.ownerId == resource.data.ownerId;
}
```
Test with the Firebase emulator's rules unit tests.

#### Mass assignment
Allow-list fields with a schema. Never write the raw body.
```ts
const UpdateProfile = z.object({ name: z.string().min(1).max(80), bio: z.string().max(500).optional() }).strict();
const data = UpdateProfile.parse(await req.json());   // role, credits, userId are rejected
await db.user.update({ where: { id: session.user.id }, data });
```

### Secrets

#### Leaked secret (in code, the client bundle or git history)
Do these in order. **Rotating the key is the fix.** Deleting the line is not.
1. **Rotate now** in the provider dashboard (Stripe, OpenAI, Supabase and so on). Give the user exact steps; you usually can't do this yourself.
2. Move the new value into server-only env vars (not `NEXT_PUBLIC_` / `VITE_` / `EXPO_PUBLIC_`), and into the hosting provider's env settings for each environment.
3. If the browser needed it, put a server route in between that calls the provider.
4. Add `.env*` (except `.env.example`) to `.gitignore`. Turn on GitHub secret scanning and push protection, or gitleaks in CI.
5. Rewriting git history (git filter-repo) is optional once the key is rotated. Tell the user it's a destructive, team-wide operation.

### Data leakage

#### API returns too much data
Send a response shape that lists exactly the fields the screen needs (a DTO or `select`), never the raw row:
```ts
const user = await db.user.findUnique({ where: { id }, select: { id: true, name: true, avatarUrl: true } });
```
For server-rendered frameworks, pass only those fields to client components. **Test:** the response for another user's public profile contains no email, phone, password hash or internal flags.

#### Account enumeration
Return the same message, with similar timing, whether or not the account exists: *"If an account exists for that email, we've sent a link."* For signup, send a "you already have an account" **email** instead of showing it on screen. Rate-limit these endpoints.

#### Private data in shared caches
Add `Cache-Control: private, no-store` to authenticated responses, and make sure CDN or framework caching (e.g. `revalidate`, edge cache rules) is off for personalised routes. **Test:** two users fetch the same URL and each sees only their own data.

### Input and injection

#### Server-side validation
One schema per endpoint, parsed on the server, and shared with the form for UX. Reject with 400 or 422 and field errors. Limit string lengths, array sizes and numbers.

#### SQL / NoSQL injection
Parameterized queries only: `` sql`select * from users where email = ${email}` `` (tagged template), `$1` placeholders, or ORM methods. For Mongo, validate that inputs are primitives (`z.string()`) so `{ "$gt": "" }` can't get through.

#### XSS
- Render user content as text by default (React escapes it automatically).
- If HTML or markdown must render: `DOMPurify.sanitize(html)`, or a markdown renderer with raw HTML disabled (`react-markdown` without `rehype-raw`).
- Validate user URLs: allow only `http:` and `https:` (blocks `javascript:`).

#### File uploads
Accept uploads through **signed upload URLs** to a **private** bucket. On the server: check size, check the real type (magic bytes, e.g. the `file-type` package), generate a random filename, and serve files via short-lived signed URLs with `Content-Disposition: attachment` for anything not shown as an image. Don't serve SVG or HTML uploads inline from your main domain.

#### Open redirect
`const next = url.startsWith("/") && !url.startsWith("//") ? url : "/";`

#### SSRF
Resolve the hostname and block private, loopback, link-local and metadata ranges before fetching. Better still, fetch only from an allow-list of domains. Turn off redirects or re-check after each one.

### Money

#### Prices from the client / payments trusted from the redirect
- The client sends a **product or price ID**. The server looks up the amount and creates the checkout session.
- Access is granted only in the **verified webhook** handler. The success page just shows "processing…" and polls your DB.

#### Webhook verification and idempotency
```ts
const raw = await req.text();                       // raw body, not parsed JSON
const event = stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(raw, req.headers.get("stripe-signature")!, process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET!);
// idempotency: a processed_events table with a UNIQUE event_id
const inserted = await db.$executeRaw`insert into processed_events (id) values (${event.id}) on conflict do nothing`;
if (inserted === 0) return new Response("ok");      // already handled
// handle the event (or enqueue it), then return 200 quickly
```
Razorpay: verify `X-Razorpay-Signature` with HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body. Paddle and Lemon Squeezy have the same pattern with their own signature headers.

#### Race conditions (credits, coupons, stock)
Use a single atomic statement or a constraint, never read-then-write:
```sql
update accounts set credits = credits - 1 where id = $1 and credits > 0 returning credits;  -- 0 rows → insufficient
create unique index one_redemption_per_user on coupon_redemptions (coupon_id, user_id);
```
For multi-step changes, use a transaction with `select … for update`.

### Reliability

#### Timeouts and error handling
```ts
const res = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) });
```
- Set timeouts on DB clients, LLM SDKs (`timeout`, `maxRetries`) and serverless functions.
- One error handler per layer: it logs the full error with a request ID to the error tracker, and returns a generic message plus the right status code to the client. Add a React error boundary or `error.tsx` for the UI.
- Replace every empty `catch {}` with handling, or rethrow.

#### Retries
Retry only idempotent operations, with exponential backoff and jitter (e.g. 0.5s, 1s, 2s ± random), at most 3–5 times. Prefer the SDK's built-in retry option.

#### Indexes and migrations
Create a migration (Prisma, Drizzle, Supabase or Rails) that adds the index, e.g. `create index concurrently if not exists idx_orders_user_created on orders (user_id, created_at desc);`. Confirm it's used with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`.

#### Backups and restore test
Turn on automated backups and point-in-time recovery in the DB provider. Then help the user **restore into a new staging DB** and check that row counts and a few records match. Record the date and the time it took.

#### Error tracking and uptime (quickest path)
Install the framework's official Sentry or PostHog wizard (`npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`), set DSNs per environment, and filter personal data out before sending. Add an external uptime check on `/` and `/api/health` with alerts to email, Slack or phone.

### Abuse and cost

#### Rate limiting
Use the platform's built-in limiter or a shared store (Upstash Ratelimit, Redis, Cloudflare rules), keyed by user ID, and by IP for anonymous traffic. Apply it to auth, OTP and SMS, email sending, uploads and AI endpoints. Return 429 with `Retry-After`. In-memory limiters don't work on serverless.

#### LLM spend caps
- Calls go only through your server, with `max_tokens` and an input length limit.
- A `usage` table (user_id, period, tokens or cost). Check and increment it atomically before each call, and refuse with a friendly "limit reached" message.
- Set a monthly budget and alert in the provider dashboard (give the user the steps).

### Headers and transport

#### Security headers (Next.js example)
```js
// next.config.js → async headers()
{ source: "/(.*)", headers: [
  { key: "Strict-Transport-Security", value: "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload" },
  { key: "X-Content-Type-Options", value: "nosniff" },
  { key: "Referrer-Policy", value: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" },
  { key: "Permissions-Policy", value: "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()" },
  { key: "Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only", value: "default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; ..." },
]}
```
Start CSP in report-only mode, fix the violations, then enforce it. Express: `helmet()`. Other platforms: use their headers config.

#### Cookies
`Set-Cookie: session=…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=…`. Move tokens out of `localStorage`, using the auth library's cookie mode.

### AI features

#### Prompt injection and unsafe output
- Treat model output like user input: sanitize before rendering, and validate with a schema before using it.
- Tools run with the end user's permissions. Destructive tools need a confirmation step in the UI.
- Scope RAG retrieval by `user_id` / `org_id` in the query itself.
- Strip or restrict external images and links in rendered output.

### Legal and privacy

#### Privacy policy that doesn't match the app
Generate a draft **from the data map** in Step 1 (each field, purpose, processor, retention, user rights, contact), not from a generic template. Mark it "DRAFT – needs legal review" and put it on the "Needs a lawyer" list.

#### Analytics before consent
Load analytics, ads pixels and session replay only after consent: keep the consent state, and initialize the scripts in a callback (or use the tool's consent mode, e.g. Google Consent Mode v2 or PostHog `opt_out_capturing_by_default`). Essential cookies stay on.

#### Account and data deletion
- Add a "Delete account" button in settings (required in mobile apps). Re-authenticate, then confirm.
- A server job deletes or anonymizes the user's rows (FK `on delete cascade` or explicit deletes), storage files, and third-party records (payment customer, email list contact, analytics person, AI provider data where possible). Revoke sessions.
- Keep only what the law requires (invoices), documented in the privacy policy.
- **Test:** after deletion, the user's data can't be found anywhere in the DB or storage.

#### GPL/AGPL dependency in closed-source code
Replace the package with a permissively licensed alternative, or isolate it. Put the license question on the "Needs a lawyer" list. Don't decide this yourself.

## Sweep patterns

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/build.py from scripts/sweep.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

`scripts/sweep.py` searches every file for these patterns (and git history for the secret ones). If Python can't run, search for them yourself, file by file, and give every match a verdict in the ledger (`FINDING <check ID>` or `RULED OUT` with the reason). A match is a lead, not a finding.

- **SECRET-AWS** → `SEC-022`: AWS access key · also in git history
  ```regex
  AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}
  ```
- **SECRET-STRIPE** → `SEC-022`: Stripe live secret or restricted key · also in git history
  ```regex
  \b[rs]k_live_[0-9A-Za-z]{10,}
  ```
- **SECRET-OPENAI** → `SEC-022`: OpenAI-style secret key · also in git history
  ```regex
  \bsk-(?:proj-|svcacct-)?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{24,}
  ```
- **SECRET-ANTHROPIC** → `SEC-022`: Anthropic API key · also in git history
  ```regex
  \bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}
  ```
- **SECRET-GOOGLE** → `SEC-022`: Google API key (may be a public Firebase web key: check) · also in git history
  ```regex
  \bAIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{35}
  ```
- **SECRET-GITHUB** → `SEC-022`: GitHub token · also in git history
  ```regex
  \b(?:gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{40,})
  ```
- **SECRET-SLACK** → `SEC-022`: Slack token · also in git history
  ```regex
  \bxox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}
  ```
- **SECRET-PRIVKEY** → `SEC-022`: Private key block · also in git history
  ```regex
  -----BEGIN (?:[A-Z]+ )?PRIVATE KEY-----
  ```
- **SECRET-JWT** → `SEC-022`: Hard-coded JWT (Supabase anon keys are public by design; service_role keys are not) · also in git history
  ```regex
  \beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}
  ```
- **SECRET-ASSIGN** → `SEC-022`: Hard-coded password, secret or token value · also in git history (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  \b(?:password|passwd|secret|api[_-]?key|access[_-]?token|auth[_-]?token|client[_-]?secret)\b["']?\s*[:=]\s*["'][^"'\s]{8,}["']
  ```
- **PUBLIC-ENV-SECRET** → `PLT-028`: Secret-looking variable with a browser-public prefix
  ```regex
  \b(?:NEXT_PUBLIC|VITE|EXPO_PUBLIC|REACT_APP|PUBLIC|NUXT_PUBLIC|GATSBY)_[A-Z0-9_]*(?:SECRET|SERVICE_ROLE|PRIVATE|PASSWORD|ADMIN)[A-Z0-9_]*
  ```
- **SERVICE-ROLE** → `BS-02`: Supabase service_role / admin SDK use (must be server-only)
  ```regex
  service_role|SERVICE_ROLE_KEY|firebase-admin
  ```
- **XSS-HTML** → `SEC-030`: Raw HTML rendering
  ```regex
  dangerouslySetInnerHTML|\.innerHTML\s*=|\.outerHTML\s*=|\bv-html\b|\{@html\b|insertAdjacentHTML
  ```
- **EVAL** → `SEC-031`: eval / new Function
  ```regex
  \beval\s*\(|\bnew Function\s*\(
  ```
- **SQL-CONCAT** → `SEC-028`: SQL built with string interpolation (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  (?:\$queryRawUnsafe|\$executeRawUnsafe|\.raw\s*\(\s*`[^`]*\$\{|`[^`\n]*\b(?:SELECT|INSERT INTO|UPDATE|DELETE FROM)\b[^`\n]*\$\{|["'][^"'\n]*\b(?:SELECT|INSERT INTO|UPDATE|DELETE FROM)\b[^"'\n]*["']\s*(?:\+|%)\s*\w|f["'][^"'\n]*\b(?:SELECT|INSERT INTO|UPDATE|DELETE FROM)\b[^"'\n]*\{)
  ```
- **CMD-EXEC** → `SEC-031`: Shell command built from variables
  ```regex
  \bexec(?:Sync)?\s*\(\s*(?:`[^`]*\$\{|["'][^"']*["']\s*\+)|\bos\.system\s*\(|subprocess\.\w+\([^)]*shell\s*=\s*True
  ```
- **TLS-OFF** → `SEC-040`: TLS certificate checking turned off
  ```regex
  rejectUnauthorized\s*:\s*false|verify\s*=\s*False|NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED|InsecureSkipVerify\s*:\s*true
  ```
- **CORS-ANY** → `SEC-037`: CORS allows any origin (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  (?:Access-Control-Allow-Origin|\borigin)["']?\s*[:,=]\s*["']\*["']|\borigin\s*:\s*true\b
  ```
- **RLS-TRUE** → `SEC-017`: Policy that allows everyone (using/with check true) (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  \b(?:using|with\s+check)\s*\(\s*true\s*\)
  ```
- **RLS-OFF** → `SEC-017`: Row-level security disabled (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  disable\s+row\s+level\s+security
  ```
- **RULES-OPEN** → `PLT-011`: Firebase rules open to everyone or time-limited test mode (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  allow\s+[\w, ]+:\s*if\s+(?:true|request\.time\s*<)
  ```
- **EMPTY-CATCH** → `BS-07`: Empty catch / except: pass (errors swallowed)
  ```regex
  catch\s*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*\{\s*\}|except[^:\n]*:\s*pass\b|\.catch\(\s*\(\s*\w*\s*\)\s*=>\s*\{\s*\}\s*\)
  ```
- **STACK-TO-USER** → `QA-022`: Error details or stack sent to the user
  ```regex
  (?:res|response|reply)\.(?:status\(\d+\)\.)?(?:json|send)\([^)\n]*(?:\.stack|err\.message|error\.message)
  ```
- **WEAK-RANDOM** → `SEC-047`: Math.random used for a token, code or ID (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  (?:token|otp|secret|password|reset|invite|nonce|code)\w*\s*[:=][^\n;]*Math\.random|Math\.random[^\n;]*(?:token|otp|secret|invite|nonce)
  ```
- **WEAK-HASH** → `SEC-041`: MD5 / SHA-1 hashing (unsafe for passwords) (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  createHash\(\s*["'](?:md5|sha1)["']|hashlib\.(?:md5|sha1)\(|\bmd5\(
  ```
- **JWT-NOVERIFY** → `SEC-004`: JWT decoded without verifying, or alg none allowed
  ```regex
  \bjwt\.decode\s*\(|algorithms\s*:\s*\[\s*["']none["']|verify_signature["']?\s*:\s*False
  ```
- **TOKEN-STORAGE** → `SEC-003`: Token stored in localStorage / sessionStorage (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  (?:localStorage|sessionStorage)\.setItem\(\s*["'`][^"'`]*(?:token|jwt|session|auth)
  ```
- **LOG-SENSITIVE** → `OPS-023`: Logging that may include secrets or personal data (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  (?:console\.(?:log|info|debug|error)|logger\.\w+|print)\s*\([^)\n]*(?:password|token|secret|authorization|cookie|apiKey|api_key|ssn|card)
  ```
- **SOURCEMAPS** → `PLT-019`: Production source maps enabled
  ```regex
  productionBrowserSourceMaps\s*:\s*true|\bsourcemap\s*:\s*true
  ```
- **DEBUG-ON** → `PLT-043`: Debug mode switched on
  ```regex
  \bDEBUG\s*=\s*True\b|app\.debug\s*=\s*True|\bdebug\s*:\s*true\b
  ```
- **HTTP-URL** → `SEC-040`: Plain http:// URL (not localhost)
  ```regex
  http://(?!localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|0\.0\.0\.0|\[::1\]|www\.w3\.org|schemas\.|json-schema\.org|example\.(?:com|org)|xmlns|ns\.adobe)[\w.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}
  ```
- **CLIENT-PRICE** → `PLT-039`: Price or amount taken from the request (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  \b(?:amount|price|unit_amount|total)\s*[:=]\s*(?:req\.body|request\.body|body|formData|params|input|args)\b
  ```
- **GOOGLE-FONTS** → `LAW-001`: Fonts loaded from Google's servers
  ```regex
  fonts\.googleapis\.com|fonts\.gstatic\.com
  ```
- **TRACKERS** → `LAW-002`: Tracker or analytics script (check it waits for consent)
  ```regex
  googletagmanager\.com|google-analytics\.com|\bgtag\(|connect\.facebook\.net|\bfbq\(|static\.hotjar\.com|clarity\.ms|snap\.licdn\.com|analytics\.tiktok\.com|cdn\.segment\.com|posthog\.init|mixpanel\.init
  ```
- **SKIPPED-TESTS** → `BS-15`: Skipped or focused tests
  ```regex
  \b(?:it|test|describe)\.(?:skip|only)\s*\(|\bx(?:it|describe)\s*\(|@pytest\.mark\.skip
  ```
- **TODO-SECURITY** → `BS-04`: TODO / FIXME about security (case-insensitive)
  ```regex
  (?:TODO|FIXME|HACK|XXX)\b[^\n]*(?:auth|secur|permission|validat|rls|secret|password|rate.?limit|sanitiz)
  ```
- **ENV-TRACKED** → `SEC-022`: a `.env` file (not `.example`) is tracked by git (`git ls-files`)
